subject: chemistry
title: Covalent bonding and dot-and-cross diagrams
key_idea: When atoms share pairs of electrons, they form covalent bonds. These bonds are strong. Covalent bonding joins non-metal atoms into small molecules, very large molecules such as polymers, or giant structures such as diamond.

blocks.text: This section explains how atoms share electrons and what substances result.

items.meaning: A shared pair of electrons between two atoms.
Two or more atoms joined together by covalent bonds.

items: Covalent bonding occurs in most non-metal elements and in compounds of non-metals.
Each shared pair gives both atoms a full outer shell.
The bonds between atoms are strong.
Hydrogen chloride is covalent: two non-metals share electrons to form molecules with no overall charge.
**Small molecules**, such as water, methane and chlorine.
**Giant covalent structures**, such as diamond and silicon dioxide.
From a diagram, a few atoms joined together is a small molecule. A repeat unit in brackets with a small n is a polymer. A continuous network of atoms is a giant structure.
A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons.
Covalent bonds join non-metal atoms into small molecules, polymers or giant structures.

blocks.text: A dot and cross diagram shows only the outer shell electrons. The shared pairs are in the overlap between the atoms.

items.text: Work out how many outer electrons each atom has from its group number.
Show the outer shells overlapping where electrons will be shared.
Place one dot and one cross in the overlap for each shared pair, so each atom reaches a full outer shell.
Every atom has a full outer shell. Only outer electrons are drawn.

diagram.alt: Pick a molecule to see its covalent bonds.

items: A single line represents a single bond (one shared pair). A double line is two shared pairs.
You can work out the molecular formula from a diagram by counting the atoms of each element.
Draw only the outer shell. Each overlap holds one shared pair, shown as a dot and a cross.
A line in a diagram stands for one shared pair.

blocks.text: Dot and cross diagrams and ball and stick models each show only some features of a molecule.

rows: Does not show the shape. It is only two-dimensional.
Not to scale. Electrons and shells are not shown. The atoms look separated by sticks.
Not three-dimensional, so the arrangement in space is incorrect.

items: Dot and cross diagrams show electrons but not shape.
Ball and stick models show the shape but not the electrons or the true size.

checks.q: Describe what is meant by a covalent bond.
checks.a: A shared pair of electrons between two atoms.

checks.q: How many covalent bonds are there in a molecule of methane, CH₄, and what does each bond contain?
checks.a: Four single covalent bonds. Each is a shared pair of electrons.

checks.q: Give one limitation of using a dot and cross diagram to represent an ammonia molecule.
checks.a: It does not show the shape of the molecule (it is only two-dimensional).

exam_phrases: hydrogen chloride is covalent (two non-metals, sharing electrons, molecules)
sodium chloride is ionic (metal and non-metal, transferring electrons)
not to scale / electrons or shells not shown
it has a giant structure / it has strong covalent bonds

mistakes.wrong: A limitation of a ball and stick model of water is that water is a liquid.
mistakes.right: Properties of water are ignored. Say the model is not to scale, is not three-dimensional, or does not show electrons or shells.

mistakes.wrong: A dot and cross diagram of ammonia shows the shape of the molecule.
mistakes.right: A dot and cross diagram does not show the shape. It is only two-dimensional.

mistakes.wrong: Silicon dioxide has a very high melting point because it has weak intermolecular forces.
mistakes.right: Silicon dioxide has a giant structure and strong covalent bonds. It does not have weak intermolecular forces.

worked_example.question:
This question is about sodium. Chlorine reacts with sodium and with hydrogen.

Compare the structure and bonding in sodium chloride and hydrogen chloride.
answer_points: Sodium chloride is ionic (metal and non-metal, electrons transferred, Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions). Hydrogen chloride is covalent (two non-metals, electrons shared, molecules with no overall charge).
Sodium chloride has a giant lattice with strong electrostatic forces acting in all directions. Hydrogen chloride has small simple molecules with weak intermolecular forces.
Similarities: both have strong bonds and full outer shells. Electrostatic forces act in sodium chloride and intermolecular forces in hydrogen chloride.
worked_example.tip: A six-mark answer marked by level. Compare both the bonding and the structure of both substances. Do not write about melting points.

exam_phrases: (two or more) atoms joined together by a covalent bond / shared pair of electrons
atoms share a pair of electrons

mistakes.wrong: A covalent bond is formed when an atom gains two electrons.
mistakes.right: Reference to ionic bonding or ions scores 0. Say a pair of electrons is shared.

mistakes.wrong: In ionic bonding, electrons are transferred from a non-metal to a metal.
mistakes.right: This is rejected. Electrons are transferred from the metal to the non-metal.

mistakes.wrong: A molecule is made of compound atoms.
mistakes.right: 'Compound atoms' is ignored. A molecule is two or more atoms joined together by a covalent bond (a shared pair of electrons).

worked_example.question:
Sodium reacts with chlorine to form sodium chloride, which contains ionic bonds.
Hydrogen reacts with chlorine to form hydrogen chloride, which contains covalent bonds.

Describe the differences between an ionic bond and a covalent bond.
answer_points: Ionic (2 marks): an electrostatic force between oppositely charged ions (anions and cations).
Covalent (2 marks): atoms share a pair of electrons.
Other credit, 1 mark each side: ionic bonds are between metals and non-metals, with electrons transferred from the metal to the non-metal. Covalent bonds form molecules and are between non-metals.
worked_example.tip: Two marks for each type of bond. Do not say electrons are transferred from a non-metal to a metal.

exam_phrases: a covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons (between atoms)
strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
lots of energy is required to overcome the forces

mistakes.wrong: A covalent bond is a shared electron.
mistakes.right: Say a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

mistakes.wrong: Magnesium sulfate has a high melting point because of strong covalent bonds.
mistakes.right: Covalent bonds, intermolecular forces or metallic bonds score 0 for an ionic compound. Say strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

worked_example.question:
Plastics are polymers. Polymers have covalent bonds between the atoms.

Explain what a covalent bond is in terms of electrons.
answer_points: A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.
worked_example.tip: One mark. Say 'shared pair of electrons'.
